highlights.title: Ila Kumar: Innovating with communities
highlights.summary: The PhD student works to give young people an active role in shaping digital technologies that can support their own well-being.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. You may not alter the images provided, other than to crop them to size. A credit line must be used when reproducing images; if one is not provided below, credit the images to "MIT."
Before Ila Kumar thinks about how to build technology, she asks a different question: What is the context that technology will operate in, and who needs to be involved in the design?

For Kumar, meaningful innovation doesn’t result from engineers or designers working in isolation. Instead, she believes the best innovations emerge when the people who stand to benefit from a technology help create it from the very beginning.

That philosophy has guided her research in the Lifelong Kindergarten group, where she works alongside young people who have experienced trauma during childhood, particularly those involved in the child welfare system, to reimagine how technology can support healing, connection, and independence.

highlights.title: 26 Years Later, Peppermint Patty's Final 'Peanuts' Strip Is Still Her Most Memorable Quote
highlights.summary: Here's an interesting fact about Peanuts: Peppermint Patty has a full canonical name, which was only ever mentioned once. It’s Patricia Reichardt, as per the strip for Jan. 15, 1972.
body: That's one of several ways in which Patty always felt like she was inhabiting a distinctly different strip than everyone else in Peanuts, and it’s not just because she and Marcie go to a different school than everyone else. In a comic where most of the characters regularly grapple with weighty issues related to theology, philosophy, and ethics, Patty gets poor grades, routinely sleeps through class, gets a D-minus on every test, and was convinced for a long time that Snoopy is just a funny-looking quiet kid instead of an actual dog.
On the other hand, Patty is a gifted athlete, and her baseball team routinely defeats Charlie Brown's. Everyone has their own talents.
Patty's academic underachievement does tend to mean that she's on the low end of the Peanuts quotability scale. When Patty's around in Peanuts, the jokes all tend to be at her own expense.

With that in mind, the most memorable line from Peppermint Patty might also be her last. Both Patty and her eternal sidekick Marcie made their final appearance in Peanuts on Jan. 2, 2000, around six weeks before the strip's conclusion.

highlights.title: A walking tour of Andalucía’s historic white villages: ‘Nightingales serenade us as we wind along lush river valleys’
highlights.summary: The famous pueblos blancos in southern Spain’s Sierra de Grazalema natural park teem with wildlife amid a limestone wonderland of peaks. ‘The wind is in from Africa / Last night I couldn’t sleep.” Joni Mitchell has ear-wormed her way into my head as my wife and I step out from Zahara de la Sierra…
body: Either way, Africa feels present as we tramp through the countryside of Andalucía, if only in the wildlife. The painted lady butterflies drifting over the flower-spangled verges, the turtle doves purring from the olive groves and the booted eagle drifting overhead: all are summer visitors recently blown in from the great continent to our south.

It’s day two of our White Villages of the Ronda Mountains walking tour, a self-guided seven-day route from On Foot Holidays that explores this alluring corner of southern Spain. We arrived yesterday by bus from Málaga, winding up through the mountains until the whitewashed dwellings of Zahara appeared like teeth in the hillside ahead. This was the first of the week’s four pueblos blancos, all tucked picturesquely into the natural park’s rugged 51,695 hectares (127,740 acres) of limestone peaks and serpentine river valleys.

I’ve walked with On Foot before, so the routine is familiar: water bottles and packed lunches stashed in daypacks, laminated map around neck on lanyard and route app open on phone (belt-and-braces navigation). Best of all, our luggage is already wending its way by taxi to the next destination.

body: The MIT Quantum Initiative (QMIT) has launched a new postdoctoral fellowship program to accelerate interdisciplinary quantum research and develop the next generation of scientific leaders working at the frontiers of quantum science and technology.

Supported by a grant from the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation, the program reflects QMIT’s vision of expanding the boundaries of quantum science by encouraging researchers to connect quantum approaches with other disciplines and emerging applications.

As opportunities in quantum research expand, investing in outstanding early-career researchers has never been more important. These fellowships are designed to help cultivate the next generation of quantum leaders, providing the resources and collaborative environment needed to advance transformative research at MIT.

body: This fixture was one of the few matches that the Gunners lost in winning the Premier League title last season but Saka's close-range effort decided what was a tight game despite an improved showing from Unai Emery's much-changed Aston Villa line-up.

Villa were four down after 31 minutes in that astonishing capitulation at Brighton on the opening weekend but they showed far more resilience against the Gunners from the outset. Emiliano Buendia crashed the ball against David Raya's crossbar on 12 minutes.

Mikel Arteta's men, unchanged from the win over Coventry, were their usual probing selves, asking searching questions from set pieces and controlling possession for long periods. But Gabriel's mistimed header was as close as they came in the first half.

Christos Tzolis was substituted at half-time having been booked and running the risk of a red card after that, but the introduction of Eberechi Eze worked out well. Arsenal ramped up the pressure in the second half with the ever-impressive Saka to the fore.

highlights.title: As the legal hunt for the GTA 6 leaker continues, Take-Two reportedly tries another more secretive Discord subpoena, this time specifying individuals
highlights.summary: Rockstar parent company Take-Two has escalated its hunt for the people behind the numerous Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks from two weeks ago. The publisher has filed a request for another subpoena, though this time it's asking the court to withhold the details from the public and keep it sealed.
body: The subpoena request, as reported by TorrentFreak, is the second one aimed at Discord. Take-Two previously filed subpoena requests targeting multiple companies whose products were used to store and disseminate the leaked GTA 6 footage, including Discord, Microsoft, and X. Following these filings, Discord said it had yet to be served, and that it would "evaluate the validity and scope before responding" if and when it was.

Take-Two's tactics seem to be changing a bit, as the company is now trying to keep the public from being able to see details of the subpoena. Unlike the original public subpoenas, no one outside the court will be able to learn details of the information Take-Two is seeking this time. The company was criticised for the scope and scale of the information it requested in Discord's initial subpoena, which targeted hundreds of thousands of users across several Discord servers where the GTA 6 leaks mainly circulated.

highlights.title: Sami Tamimi’s recipes for musabaha (warm chickpea dip) and turmeric and nigella seed flatbreads
highlights.summary: This rubbly cousin of hummus is flavourful and satisfying at any time of day, served warm, topped with a colourful salad and just made to eat with homemade flatbreads. Few things make me happier than a bowl of warm musabaha served with freshly baked bread straight from the pan.
body: When I’m short of time but craving something nourishing, full of flavour and genuinely satisfying, I turn to murabaha time and again. Unlike hummus, the chickpeas are left whole, then gently warmed and topped with a vibrant salad of spicy cherry tomatoes, fresh coriander and good olive oil. Serve with plenty of the warm flatbreads below for scooping.

Put the chickpeas in a medium saucepan with enough water just to cover them., put on a medium heat and bring to a simmer. Leave to cook for about five minutes, just to soften them a bit more, then drain, reserving about 300ml of the cooking liquid.
Meanwhile, put all ingredients for the cherry tomato salad in a medium bowl with half a teaspoon of salt, and mix well.

Put the oil in a medium saucepan on a medium heat. Add the garlic and cook, stirring often, for two minutes, until the garlic starts to colour, then add the chilli and cook for another minute. Add the drained chickpeas, the reserved cooking liquid, cumin, tahini, yoghurt, lemon juice and a teaspoon of salt, bring to a boil, then turn down the heat to low and simmer, stirring from time to time, for two minutes.

highlights.title: Apple shares ‘shocking evidence’ against former employee accused of stealing company data for OpenAI
highlights.summary: Apple says it has evidence that a former employee destroyed evidence of data theft after learning he was under investigation.
body: In its lawsuit against OpenAI, Apple filed what it calls “shocking evidence” to bolster its allegations that former employees stole trade secrets for OpenAI’s benefit. These new details emerged after the legal counsel for former Apple employee Chang Liu — who now works at OpenAI — handed over Liu’s old Apple work laptop for investigation earlier this month.

Apple now alleges that Liu used a confidential Apple circuit schematic in his work at OpenAI, as well as a tool that shares a name with an internal Apple engineering application. The company claims that OpenAI was “well-aware” of Liu’s access to Apple data, and that Liu enlisted OpenAI colleague Yu-Ting Peng to help destroy evidence in June when he learned that Apple was investigating him.

“The MacBook represents the very limited information Defendants provided so far (and only after weeks of delay), and shows Apple is not conducting ‘fishing expeditions’ but that its trade secrets are being used and evidence is being destroyed,” the filing reads.
points: Apple says it has evidence that a former employee destroyed evidence of data theft after learning he was under investigation.

highlights.title: ‘If you build something vastly smarter than you, it better be on your side’: can we stop AI from deceiving us?
highlights.summary: We are used to the idea that our fellow humans might intentionally mislead or manipulate us, but the idea that machines can now do the same is deeply unsettling. Researchers are racing to find solutions before it’s too late. The summer issue of the Long Read magazine is out now.
body: I n November 2023 – a lifetime ago in the field of artificial intelligence – some of the most powerful people in the world descended on Bletchley Park, the wartime codebreaking hub in Buckinghamshire, to talk about AI safety. In attendance were the then US vice-president, Kamala Harris, the AI bosses Sam Altman and Dario Amodei, delegations from 28 countries, two of the three so-called “godfathers” of AI, and Elon Musk.

The first iteration of ChatGPT had been released only a year earlier, and there was already plenty of evidence that AI models could be used for ill, from spreading misinformation to generating deepfakes. A presentation at the summit, however, highlighted a different issue: what if the biggest problem wasn’t to come from people misusing the technology, but from AI’s own behaviour?

highlights.title: 5 Perfect Animated Movies on Netflix That Are Better Than KPop Demon Hunters
highlights.summary: KPop Demon Hunters debuted on Netflix in June 2025, and in short order, everyone lost their minds. The movie received hundreds of millions of views and even made its way into theaters, a very rare feat for a Netflix Original that started out on the streaming platform.
body: I get it. The songs are incredibly catchy and the movie is funnier and more action-packed than anybody could have expected. But while everyone is still so excited about KPop Demon Hunters, I’d like to point out that there are other — and, dare I say, better — animated movies on Netflix as well. There are films that have stood the test of time, others that managed to bring something new to longstanding fandoms, and plenty of straight-to-Netflix flicks that didn’t make quite the same splash, but are still arguably superior.
So if you’re at all fatigued by KPop Demon Hunter -mania, I invite you to scroll right past it on Netflix and check out these five animated masterpieces instead.

KPop Demon Hunters and The Mitchells vs. the Machines actually have quite a bit in common. Both are animated films that were produced by Sony Pictures Animation and were released directly onto Netflix. The Mitchells vs. the Machines reached over 50 million views on the platform within its first month, which doesn’t really compare to the mega-hit of KPop Demon Hunters. And yet, it was easily one of the biggest releases during the pandemic.

highlights.summary: Bentley provided flights from Washington, DC, to Monterey, California, and accommodation so Ars could drive the Supersports, as well as ride in a preproduction Torcal EV, which we wrote about last week. Ars does not accept paid editorial content.
body: MONTEREY, Calif.—Last week, we brought news of the Bentley Torcal, a new electric vehicle that the luxury automaker has been cooking up at its HQ in Crewe, England. The company wants to attract new customers with its first battery EV, part of a plan to make sustainability as much a part of the brand's character as its high-end fit and finish. W12 engines have given way to V8 plug-in hybrid power, and the new Continental GT is all the better for it.

But around the same time as Ars got its first experience of that new PHEV two-door on a rather wet Spanish racetrack, some of Bentley's boffins were wondering what might happen if you also built one without the hybrid stuff.

Or all-wheel drive—something that has been a characteristic of every new road-going Bentley since the turn of the century. That would certainly cut the curb weight. So, too, would leaving out the rear seats. That sort of idea leads down a well-trodden path for some OEMs, and Porsche in particular is famous for making stripped-out road cars inspired by its race cars and making money from them, too.

highlights.title: The Hugging Face hack could indicate cultural issues at OpenAI
highlights.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. By now you’ve probably heard about last month’s major AI security incident, in which OpenAI agents escaped their sandbox and hacked into the AI platform Hugging…
body: The day before OpenAI released that report, I spoke with David Krueger, a computer science professor and prominent alignment expert who took leave from the University of Montreal to found and lead an AI safety nonprofit called Evitable. He said what he had really hoped to see in the report was an analysis of the human factors behind the incident.

“When you look at accidents and incidents, oftentimes people try to find the technical source of failure, but that can give a very inaccurate and misleading sense of why the failure occurred,” he said. “If people are just cutting corners all the time, if people are not in a culture that prioritizes safety and has appropriate incentives and structures, [accidents] are kind of bound to happen.”

The report did not meet Krueger’s hopes. Its 38 pages detail a multi-month progression of agent misbehavior that culminated in the Hugging Face hack, explore the technical reasons why that misbehavior occurred, and enumerate the steps being taken to prevent similar events in the future. But there’s no consideration of the role that company culture may have played in the incident, and the report includes few references to specific human errors.

highlights.title: 33 Years Ago, Batman’s Most Unforgettable Failure Predicted a Near-Perfect Action Series
highlights.summary: Batman has one of the most formidable rogues’ galleries in comics, but Bane understood that none of those villains had to defeat the Dark Knight to be useful. They only had to keep him busy.
body: That is the cruel genius of Batman: Knightfall Part 1: Knightfall, the new animated adaptation of the iconic ‘90s storyline in which Bane breaks Batman’s back. Bane shows up in Gotham and orchestrates a mass breakout from Arkham Asylum, which forces Batman to spend days hunting down the Joker, Scarecrow, Poison Ivy, and various other escaped inmates. By the time Bruce returns to Wayne Manor, he is physically exhausted, psychologically frayed, and completely unprepared for Bane’s ambush. Only then does Bane fight him and famously “break the Bat.”

“Hidden Inventory / Premature Death” is presented as the first five episodes of JJK season 2, though it’s a prequel arc that takes place more than a decade before the main series. In their teenage years, Satoru Gojo and Suguru Geto are assigned to protect Riko Amanai, a schoolgirl designated as the Star Plasma Vessel (a human destined to merge with Tengen to reset their immortality). Since Gojo and Geto are both already classified as Special Grade jujutsu sorcerers, attacking them directly would be foolish.

highlights.title: From the Archives: Brad Johns, the Color Czar
highlights.summary: Brad Johns, the celebrity colorist known for his “chunking” technique and influential work with Carolyn Bessette Kennedy, died last week at his home in Los Angeles. Revisit Vogue’s profile of Johns from the July 1995 issue, titled “The Color Czar.”
body: Here, revisit Vogue’ s July 1995 profile of Johns, titled “The Color Czar,” by Vanessa Friedman.

“My mission on this planet is to make people’s hair look good,” Johns says, running a hand through his own yellow-brown, blow-dried, shoulder-length locks. “Everyone’s hair, no matter what the exact tint, should be bright, beautiful, and expensive-looking.”

As it happens, this is a good time to be someone who wants to make everyone’s tresses bright and beautiful. Faux hair color, from platinum to black, has never been so big: Model Shalom stole the spring shows when she went from her natural plain brown to ebony; three of People ’s Most Beautiful People are bright fire-engine redheads; and even O.J. prosecutor Marcia Clark has used color to give her case an added boost. When glamour replaced natural as the look of choice, hair—and its power to call attention, decorate, and define—gained new potency. And that gave top colorists al-most incalculable authority.

highlights.title: The Pentagon now has its own version of ChatGPT and Grok
highlights.summary: Versions of OpenAI's ChatGPT and SpaceXAI's Grok will join Google's Gemini on the Pentagon's central portal for AI tools.
body: The Pentagon has launched versions of OpenAI’s ChatGPT and xAI’s Grok, giving 3 million civilian and military personnel access to generative AI tools that have been tailored to “warfighter needs.”
ChatGPT Mil and Grok for Government — custom versions of the popular consumer generative AI tools — are now part of GenAI.mil, a centralized, secure portal launched last year.

GenAI.mil, which offered Google Gemini when it first launched, is designed to give Department of Defense employees access to commercial frontier AI models without sending sensitive government data through ordinary consumer channels. In particular, the official military version is exempt from the data collection that is difficult to avoid in consumer tech products.

And according to the Department of Defense, the generative AI portal has proven popular. GenAI.mil has already onboarded more than 1.7 million unique users out of the department’s 3 million personnel, according to the department.

highlights.title: Can Aaron Esh Make AllSaints Cool Again?
highlights.summary: CEO Peter Wood met Aaron Esh in a chance encounter at the Fashion Awards in 2024. Now, he’s giving the designer full creative freedom to reset the label.
body: It’s midday on a Wednesday at AllSaints HQ, a former industrial warehouse in London’s East End that, for some three decades, has housed the British premium brand. Designer Aaron Esh, a city native known for his buzzy namesake label, is finalizing almost a year’s worth of work as AllSaints chief creative officer, ahead of the big reveal on September 1. The question is, can Esh make AllSaints cool again?

Across the globe, current brand sentiment toward AllSaints varies, a company representative shared. In Asia, the positioning is stronger, and the brand is considered high end. But for many Brits, AllSaints had its heyday during the 2000s and early 2010s, when it was associated with the typical tropes of indie sleaze style — “Jesus Loves” studded belts, military boots, and distressed jeans — as well as the popular youth culture TV series of that era, Skins. Across the rest of the world, it holds a stronger image.
A big part of Esh’s vision lies in elevating the brand in both quality and look.
